summary:
Abbas on Mars is an interactive educational platform that transforms learning about the Red Planet into an exciting space exploration adventure. Through the story of Abbas, an astronaut trying to survive on Mars with the help of his robotic companion, Spirit, users explore the planet, discover its geological features, and learn about its scientific history.

Our project combines a 3D exploration game, an interactive Mars map, and a digital comic book to create an engaging learning experience. Users can complete missions, collect oxygen, scan rock samples, answer scientific questions, and explore five important Martian locations.

Our goal is to make space science more accessible and enjoyable by combining technology, storytelling, and interactive learning, inspiring users to discover more about Mars and its mysteries.
details:
Abbas on Mars – An Interactive Journey to Explore the Red Planet

Abbas on Mars is an interactive educational web platform designed to transform space science learning into an immersive exploration experience. Our project combines storytelling, 3D gaming, interactive maps, and digital comics to help users discover Mars in an engaging and enjoyable way.

How Does It Work?

The experience follows Abbas, an astronaut who crashes on Mars and must survive while exploring the planet with the help of his robotic companion, Spirit.

The platform consists of four main components:

  1. Interactive Website: Introduces the mission, presents different Martian locations, and guides users through the exploration experience using animations and interactive elements.
  2. 3D Exploration Game: Built using Three.js, this first-person game allows users to explore Jezero Crater, navigate the Martian terrain, collect oxygen canisters, scan rock samples, and answer scientific questions. Correct answers restore oxygen and help users complete their mission.
  3. Mars Survey Atlas: An interactive map featuring five important Martian locations: Jezero Crater, Valles Marineris, Olympus Mons, the North Polar Cap, and Gale Crater. Users can explore each location, discover geological information through conversations between Abbas and Spirit, and collect scientific findings in a personal archive.
  4. Digital Comic Book: A 31-page interactive comic that tells the exploration story through visual storytelling, animated page transitions, chapter navigation, and interactive controls.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our project makes complex scientific concepts easier to understand through interactive learning and gamification. It encourages curiosity, critical thinking, scientific exploration, and independent learning. It also introduces users to Martian geology, ancient water systems, planetary landscapes, and the scientific search for evidence of past microbial life.

Creativity and Innovation

Instead of presenting scientific information through traditional educational materials, we turn learning into a story-driven adventure. Users do not simply read about Mars; they explore its environments, complete missions, interact with scientific information, and build their own exploration archive.

Technologies and Tools Used

  • HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for development.
  • Three.js for 3D environments and exploration.
  • SVG for interactive maps.
  • Canvas API for animated visual effects.
  • Local Storage for saving exploration progress.
  • Google Fonts for typography.

We also considered responsive design, accessibility, user engagement, and performance across different screen sizes.

Our Vision

Our vision is to make space exploration and planetary science accessible to more people by combining technology, creativity, and education, inspiring the next generation to explore the universe and discover the science behind other worlds.
dataRefs: How we used it in the map: We relied on this platform as our primary source for geographic, topographic, and terrain data of the Martian surface.  * What we discovered from it:    * In the Olympus Mons region: We discovered extreme elevation differences (over 21 km) and steep, hazardous cliffs around its base that prevent direct landing or safe walking routes.    * In the Amazonis Planitia plains: We found that it is one of the flattest and smoothest regions on Mars, making it an ideal and safe corridor for rover and astronaut navigation.    * In Crater regions (volcanic and impact craters): We were able to accurately map their coordinates and depths to use them as geological exploration points or natural shelters.

How we used it in the map: We used this database to define the scientific objectives of the map and identify priority zones currently targeted by NASA's ongoing research.  * What we discovered from it:    * We discovered that future missions focus on areas that combine ease of movement (such as Amazonis) with high geological value (such as crater rims and volcanic regions) to search for subsurface water traces and analyze soil mineral composition.    * Funded research insights helped us establish route design requirements that match the operational limits of rovers and spacesuits across rugged terrain.

How we used it in the map: We used the medical and biological research papers in this library to add "human safety standards" and designate safe zones for astronauts on the map.  * What we discovered from it:    * We discovered that extremely high altitudes, like the summit of Olympus Mons, have a much thinner atmosphere, which dangerously increases astronaut exposure to cosmic and solar radiation.    * Conversely, we found that lower elevations and deep craters offer better natural radiation shielding, and the studies helped us determine the maximum safe distance and physical exertion time for astronauts operating under Martian gravity.
projectRefs: What the Source Provided: 3D images and topographic data captured by the High-Resolution Stereo Camera (HRSC) aboard the European "Mars Express" spacecraft, covering the crater and its broad geological surroundings.  * Key Findings/Documentation for the Map: Detection of ancient water drainage channels feeding into and flowing out of the crater, confirming the past existence of an integrated water system in the area and helping map the boundaries of clay deposits formed by ancient flowing water. 2. Olympus Mons  * Verified Source: German Aerospace Center (DLR - Planetary Research)

What the Source Provided: Digital Terrain Models (DTMs) and detailed perspective maps for analyzing mountain slopes and the scarp edges surrounding the volcano's base.  * Key Findings/Documentation for the Map: Explanation of the steep rocky scarp surrounding the volcano's base, reaching up to 7 kilometers in height. The data revealed that this scarp resulted from massive landslides and potentially the interaction of ancient lava with subsurface water ice. 3. Amazonis Planitia  * Verified Source: The University of Arizona (HiRISE Operations Center)

What the Source Provided: An archive of ultra-high-resolution imagery (up to 0.25 meters per pixel) along with measurement and analysis tools for surface soil and rock properties across the plain.  * Key Findings/Documentation for the Map: Discovery that the plain's smooth surface contains intricate patterns of sand dunes and thermal contraction cracks, proving continuous wind activity and seasonal temperature variations that shape the surface and keep its soil dynamic. 4. Comprehensive Interactive Map & Geographic Integration  * Verified Source: American Geophysical Union / Open Planetary Project (Mars Map)

What the Source Provided: Open-source GIS map layers combining official nomenclature approved by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) with topographic data.  * Key Findings/Documentation for the Map: Integration of the precise coordinates of the three landmarks (Jezero, Olympus, and Amazonis) into a unified coordinate system, allowing for an accurate comparison of elevations and slopes between the highest volcanic peak and the flattest plains on the planet.
